Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:83: From here you shall see how great is the virtue of one who occupies himself with Torah from midnight, that he is fittingly called "master of Torah," for he unites with the Torah, who is a king's daughter - and without doubt, whoever is constant in this measure shall have the secrets of Torah revealed to him, for a woman reveals her secrets only to her husband.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:84: And in the Midrash "Ve'eleh HaDevarim" on the verse (Deuteronomy 30:11), "for this commandment," and so on, "it is not too wondrous for you," and so on - Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said, to what is the matter comparable? To a king's daughter whom no one knew, and the king had one beloved friend who would come to the king at every hour, and the king's daughter would stand before him. The king said to him, see how I cherish you, that no creature knows my daughter, yet she stands before you. So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: see how beloved you are to Me, that no creature in My palace knows the Torah, and to you I have given it, as it is said (Job 28:21), "and it is hidden from the eyes of all living" - but you, "it is not too wondrous for you, but the matter is very near to you." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, My children, if the words of Torah are near to you, I too shall call you near, as it is written (Psalms 148:14), "for the children of Israel, a people near to Him" - to this point. And since the Torah is compared to a king's daughter, without doubt a king's daughter reveals herself more to her beloved at night than by day, for at night is the way of modesty, and it is written (Proverbs 11:2), "and with the modest is wisdom."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:85: And as it appears in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 97b), found among us in manuscript, whoever reads Torah from midnight onward for the sake of unification is called one who occupies himself with Torah for its own sake - it says there: and there is none who strives in Torah to raise the Shechinah from exile and to join her with her husband, for their eyes are closed, their hearts sealed - and therefore a voice goes out every night, when the Holy One, blessed be He, descends into the Garden of Eden, for those who ascend, and that voice says, "what shall I call?" (Isaiah 40:6) - go and say, let them strive in Torah to join the Shechinah with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the manner of David, who said (Psalms 132:4), "if I give sleep to my eyes," and so on, "until I find a place for the LORD" - and he would strive in Torah, of which it is said (Proverbs 1:8), "and forsake not your mother's teaching," with her husband, and so on. And it says further there, and concerning those who do not strive in it for its own sake, the holy spirit, which is the Shechinah, does not rest upon them - and we copied the rest of his wording in the Gate of Love, chapter 8.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:86: And so he said in the Tikkunim (page 2a): and those who do not strive in it for its own sake, of them it is said (Deuteronomy 22:7), "you shall surely send away the mother" - "et" [the direct-object marker] to include the Name YHVH, which departs with her from that person - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:87: And the essence of occupying oneself with Torah for its own sake is to read it out of love, for we are commanded several times in the commandment of love - and when a person rises for the love of the supernal union, and pictures the union with his wife at midnight, how it is out of love, so shall the love of the Creator burn in his heart, all the more so since he is a Torah scholar, as we explained above. And so he said in the Zohar (Parashat Vaera, page 30a): when the night is divided, those whose desire is to remember the Holy One, blessed be He, constantly, do not give their heart rest, and so on - and this is the lover whose heart goes burning for his beloved, that he neither slumber nor sleep from the abundance of love for her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:88: And though we have elaborated on the virtue of the occupation with Torah at night, one must also occupy oneself with it by day, as explained in the teaching we copied above from Parashat Beshalach (page 46a), and so it is explained in the Midrash Shir HaShirim Rabbah (5:10), in these words, on the verse (Song of Songs 5:11), "his locks are curled [taltalim], black as a raven" - Rabbi Azarya said, even matters that you see as thorns [kotzin] in the Torah, are heaps upon heaps [tilei tilim] - through whom are they established? "Black as a raven" - through one who rises early and stays late [ma'ariv]. Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish [disagreed]: Rabbi Yochanan said, there is no song of Torah except at night, for it is said (Proverbs 31:15), "and she rises while it is still night," and it is written (Lamentations 2:19), "arise, cry out in the night." Rabbi Shimon said, [it is] by day and night, for it is said, "and she rises while it is still night," and "you shall meditate on it day and night" (Joshua 1:8). Reish Lakish said, and so Rabbi Yochanan taught us, that there is no song of Torah except at night. Reish Lakish said, when I would toil in Torah by day, it would illuminate me at night, as it is said, "you shall meditate on it day and night" - to this point. And Reish Lakish's saying, "when I would... it would illuminate," it appears to me that its secret is like the light of a lamp shining within a glass lantern, and like the sun, which withdraws from shining by day and shines by night through the moon and stars - so the occupation with Torah by day is the secret of the light of the sun, and therefore causes an illumination to be drawn to the soul at night. And this dispute of Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish is brought in another manner in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah, end of Parashat Ki Tisa).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:89: And so, regarding rising at midnight, one who does not occupy himself with Torah by day with desire, and does not direct his intent in it to the secret of unification, will not be constant in it - and so in his prayers, he should likewise direct his intent to the secret of unification, and when lying down he should think of love for the Shechinah, and think in his mind, when will the time of love come, to do the will of his Maker - and so King David, peace be upon him, would say (Psalms 101:2), "I will contemplate the way of the blameless; when will You come to me," and so on. And when the soul returns to the body at midnight, the Shechinah comes with it, so that unification be performed through that soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:90: And after we have explained the obligation incumbent upon us to rise, and how great the reward is, we wish to explain further reflections according to reason, in order to hasten the person. Rabbeinu Yonah wrote at the beginning of the Book of Fear, that in the morning, when a person awakens from his sleep, it is fitting that he place the love of the Creator in his heart, that He did good to him in restoring his soul to him - for how many lay on their beds and did not rise - and concerning this we say, "who restores souls to dead corpses" - and then he should not linger on his bed in a lazy manner, but think, were they calling him to the king's service, how quickly he would rise, or were a fire to break out in the courtyard. And though these words of his concern the matter of prayer, it is fitting that we learn from them concerning rising at midnight, for we have already written that at midnight the Holy One, blessed be He, restores the souls to the bodies so that they occupy themselves with Torah, so that he not have "an opening of the mouth," and so on - if so, it is fitting to take to heart these reflections mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:91: And these two aspects are because of fear, for it is fitting to place upon oneself the fear of Heaven like the fear of flesh and blood, for one who transgresses the king's command deserves punishment. And it is fitting to think that if he does not repent and rise to occupy himself with Torah, he will fall into the fire of Gehinnom - for every night he does not rise, he is destined to be held accountable for having blemished his days, since the repair of the night is through the occupation with Torah, and since he has not repaired the attribute of night, his days are found lacking and blemished. And you already know what is said in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 224a), "woe to him who diminishes his days above," and so on, as we copied his wording in the Gate of Fear, chapter 10.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:92: And so they explained, concerning the punishment of one who does not rise, there (beginning of Parashat Lech Lecha), in these words: come and see, at the time midnight is aroused, and the Holy One, blessed be He, enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous, all the trees in the Garden of Eden sing and praise before Him, as it is written (1 Chronicles 16:33), "then shall the trees of the forest sing before the LORD," and so on - and a herald calls loudly and says, to you the supernal holy ones say, who among you lets spirit enter his ears to hear, and his eyes are open to see, and his heart is open to know, at this hour, and so on - woe to those who sleep in their holes, who do not know and do not observe, or they shall rise in the judgment of the reckoning that is appointed, and so on - and they elaborated further there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:93: And what reckoning shall a person give if he does not strive to fulfill this matter - behold it is written (Malachi 1:6), "a son honors his father, and a servant his master; if then I am a father, where is My honor, and if I am a master, where is My fear" - behold, we are called sons and we are called servants: "you are children to the LORD your God" (Deuteronomy 14:1); "for the children of Israel are servants to Me, they are My servants" (Leviticus 25:55) - behold, we are obligated to honor our Father in Heaven through Torah, which is called, "the wise shall inherit honor" (Proverbs 3:35), and whoever does not rise to occupy himself with Torah, they said of him, "his spirit was not aroused... he did not attend to the honor of his Master" - and behold, everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created, He created only for His honor (Avot, chapter 6, mishnah 12) - if so, what benefit is there in his creation, after he does not give honor to his Creator?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:94: And so the aspect of fear - that He is Master over us, that He rules over us, and into His hand we entrust our souls, and it is in His hand to remove them in an instant, as it is written (Job 12:10), "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing." And according to the secret, since the attribute of fear is the Shechinah, and she is the attribute of night, and to her we entrust our souls, one must fear her judgments - and therefore they said in Sanhedrin (92a): Rabbi Elazar said, any house in which words of Torah are not heard at night, fire consumes it, as it is said (Job 20:26), "all darkness is hidden for his treasures, a fire not fanned shall consume him; it shall go ill with him who remains in his tent" - and "remains" [sarid] refers only to a Torah scholar, as it is said (Joel 3:5), "and among the remnant [sridim] whom the LORD calls." And this fire is not literal, but rather the secret of the judgment that melts upon him. And for this reason, those occupied with Torah at night are called "those who fear," and concerning them it is said (Psalms 147:11), "the LORD is pleased with those who fear Him," and also, "He has given food to those who fear Him" (Psalms 111:5).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:95: Also, among the things one must take to heart is that twice each day we recite the Shema, in which it is written (Deuteronomy 6:5), "and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart," and so on - and included in this love is rising at midnight for love of the Shechinah, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 68a) on the verse (Isaiah 26:9), "my soul yearns for You in the night," and it is written (Proverbs 8:17), "I love those who love Me, and those who seek Me diligently shall find Me." And so we say (Numbers 15:40), "and be holy to your God" - and the holiness of one who banishes sleep from his eyes is included in these holinesses, that he not liken himself to the people of the world who sleep all night, but liken himself to the people of the supernal world, the holy righteous who rise at midnight to occupy themselves with Torah - and we were warned not to be drawn after the counsel of our inclination (Deuteronomy 11:16), "take heed to yourselves, lest your heart be enticed," and so on. It follows that whoever does not rise to occupy himself with Torah at night nullifies from himself love, fear, and holiness. And one who delights in nighttime sleep, it is possible that they defile him with a seminal emission, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Bereshit, end of page 19), in these words: further, the pleasures of people who delight in nighttime sleep - male and female demons emerge from them - to this point. And in chapter 18 he explained the reason for this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:96: And further, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, warned us concerning sleep, and said that Torah is acquired through minimizing sleep (Avot, chapter 6, mishnah 6), and they said in Bereshit Rabbah (parashah 44:17), on the verse (Genesis 15:12), "and it was, when the sun was about to set," and so on, in these words: Rabbi Yehoshua of Sichnin in the name of Rabbi Levi - the beginning of the collapse is sleep: he sleeps and does not toil in Torah, he sleeps and does not do his work - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:97: And further, in the Baraita of Tractate Kallah (chapter 4), in these words: learn to accept all the words of Torah in suffering - we have learned, whoever sustains himself with the words of Torah, the Torah does not attach itself to him - there [i.e., "life"] refers to the pleasure of the soul, here [in Torah] to sleep - to this point. And what is difficult about "whoever sustains himself with the words of Torah" - it means one who indulges himself while occupied with Torah, and so they expounded in Tanchuma, beginning of Parashat Noach: "and it is not found in the land of the living" (Job 28:13) - it is found only in one who "puts himself to death" over it. And it answered "there is the pleasure of the soul" - the explanation of the verse "and it is not found in the land of the living" is concerning the pleasure of the soul, namely eating and drinking; and what it says, "learn to accept the words of Torah," is the suffering of banishing sleep from his eyes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:98: And so King Solomon, peace be upon him, warned us concerning this, in saying (Proverbs 20:13), "do not love sleep, lest you come to poverty; open your eyes, and be satisfied with bread." And though the plain sense of the verse concerns monetary poverty, it is also explained in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu Zuta (chapter 14) concerning poverty of Torah - it says in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, and so on, on this verse, that "bread" refers only to Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 9:5), "come, eat of my bread," and so on, and it says (Isaiah 50:4), "the LORD God has given me a tongue of the learned," and so on - from this you learn that the words of Torah are absorbed only by one who wearies himself with them. So the holy spirit would announce to Torah scholars and say, my children, although I have given you good in this world, I do not need to say [what awaits you] in the World to Come, for you have a great reward - do not disdain My Torah, and do not indulge in eating and drinking - to this point. And the intent of saying "do not disdain My Torah and do not indulge," and so on, is because food brings sleep, and one who indulges in eating and drinking indulges in sleep, and is found idle from the words of Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:99: And so it is understood from the words of Tanna DeVei Eliyahu before this, which says, in these words: who impoverishes himself? Whoever indulges in eating and drinking, as it is said (Proverbs 23:21), "for the glutton and the drunkard shall come to poverty" - and it says, "do not love sleep, lest you come to poverty; open your eyes, and be satisfied with bread," and "bread" refers only to Torah, and so on. And what connection does the verse "do not love sleep, lest you come to poverty" have to the verse "for the glutton and the drunkard shall come to poverty"? Rather, the intent of saying "who impoverishes himself" is not concerning monetary poverty but poverty of Torah, and he learns by verbal analogy that just as the verse "do not love sleep, lest you come to poverty" is about poverty of Torah - and the proof is from its end, "open your eyes" - so the verse "for the glutton and the drunkard shall come to poverty" is about poverty of Torah, for the reason explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:100: It follows that whoever wishes to rise at midnight must not indulge in heavy eating, which increases sleep, and likewise should be careful not to become drunk with wine, and should also not indulge in drinking water, for drinking much water naturally increases sleep - and especially one who drinks water upon rising early increases sleep upon himself. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said concerning Ezekiel, of whom it was said (Ezekiel 4:11), "and you shall drink water by measure, a sixth of a hin; from time to time you shall drink" - for "measure" [mesurah] is a small measure, one-thirtieth of a log, and what it says, "a sixth of a hin," it does not mean that the "measure" is a sixth of a hin, but rather that he should drink no more than a sixth of a hin from time to time [i.e., in a day], and from that sixth of a hin he should drink by small measures, little by little, so as not to satisfy himself with water at any one time - so Radak, peace be upon him, wrote in his explanation of the verse. And a sixth of a hin measures twelve eggs' volume, for a hin is twelve logs, and a log is six eggs' volume - this is the measure a person should drink from time to time, and drink it by small measures, little by little - and it is possible that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, intended this in saying (Avot, chapter 6, mishnah 4), "and drink water by measure."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:101: And close to this, Rabbi Yosef Yaavetz, of blessed memory, wrote in his commentary on the chapters [of Avot, ibid.], in these words: and further, bread with salt is good for memory, and water causes forgetting; and one who lies at the foot of the bed and on a couch of Damascus [luxury] finds it hard in his eyes to rise at dawn to study Torah - but one who suffers for the sake of Torah shall preserve it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:102: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 21b) on the verse (Proverbs 8:12), "I, wisdom, dwell with prudence [ormah]" - Rabbi Asi bar Chanina said, the words of Torah endure only in one who makes himself "naked" [arum] over them, as it is said, "I, wisdom, dwell with prudence [ormah/nakedness]" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:103: Also, it is fitting that he be content with whatever food he finds ready at night, and not delay until a dish is cooked for him, for then he is found to be neglecting his Maker's service for love of his body. Also, whoever wishes to fulfill this measure, to be among the Torah scholars who "castrate" themselves from Sabbath night to Sabbath night, must be careful not to eat meat and wine at night on the six weekdays, lest he come to heat and emit seed in vain - unless he fasts, for then he will not come to this, since the affliction of the fast will nullify his strength and he will not come to heat. And this matter depends on each person's nature - there is one whose nature is cold, that even if he eats meat and drinks wine he will not come to heat, and there is one whose nature is hot - and each one should examine his own nature and guard himself so that his gain not come out through his loss.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:104: Also, it is fitting to take to heart that it is fitting to repent, to repair the rest of the nights remaining of his days, so that he not be held accountable for them - and if he repents properly, it is possible that what he blemished in several nights when he did not occupy himself with Torah will not be held against him, for the night in which he did not occupy himself with Torah has passed and can no longer be repaired.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:105: And one cannot say that if he did not occupy himself with Torah at night he shall occupy himself with it by day, for where he blemished, he must repair - as it says in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas, page 217a) on the verse (Numbers 25:4), "and hang them up before the LORD, opposite the sun," the words of Rabbi Shimon, peace be upon him, in these words: rather, from here we learn - in the place where a person sins against the Holy One, blessed be He, in that same place he must make his repair for his soul; they sinned in the holy covenant, which is called "sun," therefore the judgment and repair is "opposite the sun" and not in another place - from here, that a person need not repair his soul except in that place where he sinned against it, and whoever does not do so has no repair at all, properly - to this point. Behold, in the place where he blemished, there the repair is needed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:106: And it appears to me that if he blemished the attribute of night through a seminal emission, his repair is to banish sleep from his eyes at night through the occupation with Torah - and this is when the emission occurs from midnight onward, as explained above, "people who delight in nighttime sleep," and so on. And in order not to have a seminal emission before midnight, it is good that he occupy himself with Torah before lying down, as it says in Tractate Berachot (14a): Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, whoever satisfies himself with words of Torah and then retires, they do not bring him evil tidings, as it is said (Proverbs 19:23), "and satisfied, he shall lodge, untouched by evil" - and it is already known (Zohar, Parashat Shelach, page 158a) that one who emits seed in vain is called "evil."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:107: Also, it is fitting to take to heart what Scripture says (Micah 6:3), "My people, what have I done to you, and how have I wearied you? Testify against Me." Behold, we see that the king's servants have several kinds of service imposed upon them, and they serve with a good heart and with joy - and it is fitting to think, were he a captive - and it is known that captives have a heavy yoke placed upon them - so it is fitting that he accept upon himself the yoke of Torah to rise for the service of our King, even though it be hard, all the more so, since if a servant's master were to say to him, for love of me, do such and such to give me satisfaction, how that servant would hasten - and behold, the Shechinah says (Song of Songs 8:13), "companions listen for your voice, let me hear it."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:108: Further, he shall picture: were a messenger of the king to come to call him to the king's house, especially if he is a prince and honored, how fitting it would be to hasten to rise quickly. So he should think that the messenger of the King is his soul, returning to call him to rise and occupy himself with Torah - especially since the Shechinah herself is what restores souls at this hour - and it is fitting that he rise with alacrity, since a prince and master awaits him. And it is fitting that he rise with joy and love, when he thinks that he stands before the Cause of all causes, before all the righteous in the Garden of Eden, for there is no curtain between us and Him, since He restores our souls to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:109: And it is fitting for every person to think of the resurrection of the dead performed upon him, along the lines of what we say, "who restores souls to dead corpses" - especially since He restores his soul anew, as it is said (Lamentations 3:23), "new every morning" - and therefore it is fitting that he rise with joy, and not think, in his rising, that a heavy yoke is upon him, for he is punished, as it is written (Deuteronomy 28:47), "because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy" - for since he stands before the supernal King and before all His servants and ministers, and the King says to him, I wish that you be among My servants who sing before Me, who is the evil servant who would not wish to be among the king's servants, and say in his heart, from where did I merit to be among the members of the king's palace who stand before him? And he shall think of the surpassing goodness of the Creator toward him, as we elaborated in the Gate of Love, chapter 2, and it is fitting that he not be ungrateful, but hasten to the service of his King, and liken himself to a servant whose master paid his wages in advance, with a pleasant face - for it is fitting that the servant hasten to work in return for what he enjoyed, with a pleasant face and out of love - and the teaching of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, is already known (cf. Tanchuma, Emor 7), "who has preceded Me, that I should repay him" (Job 41:3), which we copied in the Gate of Love, chapter 2.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:110: And he shall think that were he digging and finding a hidden treasure, how he would rise with alacrity - by this measure shall be the service of the Creator, as it is said (Proverbs 2:4), "if you seek it as silver, and search for it as for hidden treasures, then you shall understand the fear of the LORD." Behold, the good of this world is entirely passing and lost, while the good of the World to Come stands and endures forever, and the words of Torah are more precious than gold, than much fine gold.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:111: And if he awakens from his sleep at night and turns his heart to idle matters, he is liable in his soul, for he is obligated to rise and occupy himself with Torah, and if he does not rise he mocks the reward of the King - along the lines of what the pious Yaavetz, peace be upon him, explained concerning "two who sit together without words of Torah between them, this is a session of scoffers" (Avot, chapter 3, mishnah 2), which he explained in its place in the chapters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:112: Therefore it is fitting that he rise with alacrity, and not linger on his bed in a lazy manner, thinking about what he dreamed, so that he return to sleep - and any dream that is from the side of holiness, forgetfulness shall not rule over it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:113: And should you say, behold, there are those who are not aroused at midnight - it may be said that this is from the paucity of the arousal of their deeds and their Torah. And the reason is that when the soul returns at night to its place, the Shechinah is aroused through it and adorns herself for the union, from the Torah and good deeds he occupied himself with by day, and afterward returns to her place - and so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 213b), in these words: at night he should set his will, for he has departed from this world, and his soul goes out from him and returns to the Master of all - because every single night is a secret of secrets, known to the wise of heart. This lower firmament, in the secret of that point that stands as we have said - that firmament is comprised from above and below, and its foundation is below, like this lamp, whose black light ascends to unite with the white light, its foundation being below in that wick with oil - so too below, in that point: by day it is included from above, at night it is included from below, from the souls of the righteous.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:114: And it says further there, that the angel Suriya is appointed to raise the souls of the righteous every night as an offering to the Holy One, blessed be He, and he smells the souls, along the lines of how King Messiah will in the future smell, as it is written (Isaiah 11:3), "and he shall smell in the fear of the LORD" - and the intent is that he smells them and their deeds, to see if they are fit to ascend above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:115: And it says further there, this secret to the master of judgment: when this point is impregnated, like a woman who becomes pregnant, she enjoys that pleasure of the soul that is included from this world, from those deeds and from that Torah he strove in by day, and she takes that will of this world, and through it she enjoys with gladness, and is included from every side - afterward she brings them forth and gives birth to them as before, and the soul is new now as before, and this is the secret of "new every morning" (Lamentations 3:23) - new, certainly, as has been said - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:116: And in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, page 119b) it says that one's soul must ascend every night through the Torah and commandment he occupied himself with by day, and it explains there, concerning the Torah, that it is the Ten Commandments, and so on, and concerning the commandment of tefillin, and so on - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:117: And so, one should be careful to precede the evening prayer with Torah, as they said (Berachot 4b): a person comes from his work in the evening - if he is accustomed to reading, he reads; to studying, he studies; and let him not say, I will eat a little and sleep a little and then pray - for whoever transgresses the words of the Sages is liable to death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:118: And the order of the night is thus: before lying down, he should examine his deeds, what he did that day, and write down his deeds in allusion so as not to forget them, to fulfill "and my sin is ever before me" (Psalms 51:5) - and so it is written in Sefer Chasidim (siman 21). And in the Zohar (Parashat Korach, page 178a), in these words, on the verse (Ecclesiastes 9:10), "for there is no deed, nor reckoning, nor knowledge," and so on - he says, in these words: whoever has a good deed, or is a master of reckoning, this has been established, that every single night, before he lies down and before he sleeps, a person should make a reckoning of the deeds he did that whole day, and repent of them, and ask for mercy concerning them - why at that hour? Because at that hour the tree of death rests in the world, and all the people of the world taste the taste of death, and at that hour he must make a reckoning of his deeds and confess them, because it is the hour of death - and these are called "masters of reckoning" - to this point. And so it is also explained there (Parashat Vayeshev, page 191a). And concerning the matter of confession, there are further particulars explained in the Zohar (Parashat Tzav, in the Ra'aya Meheimna, page 33a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:119: And it is very good that he weep over his sins while confessing his sins - for when his soul ascends through a tear, certainly it shall ascend above in holiness, since all the gates are locked except the gates of tears (cf. Berachot 32b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:120: And afterward he should say "Ana Bekoach" ["We beseech You, by the great strength of Your right hand, release the captive"], and so on, in which is the Name of forty-two, in the initial letters, and it is explained in the Tikkunim that the property of the Name of forty-two is to raise the soul above and hide it from all destroying angels - and this matter is found among us in manuscript (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 94a), in these words: and these seven words - Alef-Bet-Gimel Yud-Tav-Tzadi, Kuf-Resh-Ayin Shin-Tet-Nun, Nun-Gimel-Dalet Yud-Chaf-Shin, Bet-Tet-Resh Tzadi-Tav-Gimel, Chet-Kuf-Bet Tet-Nun-Ayin, Yud-Gimel-Lamed Peh-Zayin-Kuf, Shin-Kuf-Vav Tzadi-Yud-Tav - concerning them it is said (Isaiah 6:2), "each had six wings, six wings," and so on. And this Name has the property of covering the soul when it ascends above every single night, to testify concerning the person's good deeds, from the destroying angels and from all harmful spirits, demons, liliths, and evil spirits, and through them it flies upward - with two letters of each name it covers its face from them, with two letters it covers its feet, and with two letters it flies upward, and likewise for the ru'ach, and likewise for the nefesh. (And there is a Name of forty-two in the form of a wax seal, and there is a Name of forty-two that is the image of the King engraved upon the seal, and there is a Name of forty-two that is His image, which is YHVH, Yud-Heh-Vav-Heh spelled with alefs: Yud-Vav-Dalet Heh-Alef Vav-Alef-Vav Heh-Alef - the Name of forty-two, which is "Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh," the figure of forty-two in wax upon this writing, Alef-Bet-Gimel-Yud-Tav-Tzadi) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:121: And after he confesses, he should intend to raise an offering to the LORD, and that his soul become, for the Shechinah, "female waters" until midnight, and at midnight the Shechinah shall restore his soul to him - and this is the intent of "into Your hand I entrust my spirit" (Psalms 31:6).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:122: Also, it is fitting to prepare a rooster to wake him at midnight - for we find that Rabbi Akiva, when traveling on the road, would take a rooster with him, as explained in the chapter "HaRo'eh" (Berachot 60b). Also, it says in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 92b), in these words: Rabbi Abba was coming from Tiberias to the house of his father-in-law's family, and Rabbi Yaakov son of Rabbi was with him - they happened upon the village of Tarsha, and when they wished to lie down, Rabbi Abba said to the master of the house, are there roosters here? The master of the house said to him, why? He said to him, because I intend to rise at exactly midnight, and so on. Behold, these sages did not rely on their wisdom and piety that they would awaken at midnight, and needed assistance - all the more so we.
